sentence: This project searches for small molecules that block a step where a coronavirus protease cuts itself free from a larger precursor.
This project makes soluble envelope glycoprotein trimers and related reagents, and supplies them to other research teams.
This project follows patients with a genetic disease caused by a change in the valosin-containing protein gene to see how the disease progresses over time.
This project builds a test that finds hepatitis C virus in outpatient clinics and gives results in less than 30 minutes.
This project builds a service that finds the targets on cancer cells that cytotoxic T lymphocytes attack, to guide personalized cancer immunotherapies.
This project builds a way to measure lipids and RNA in single cancer cells inside intact tissue samples using microscopy.
This project studies how Epstein-Barr Virus latency, epigenetics and metabolism drive epithelial cancers and looks for weak points to treat them.
This project supports work in genetics and genomics that helps explain biological processes and disease diagnosis.
This project monitors antibiotic resistance in bacteria found in animals through culture and susceptibility testing.
This project tries to find out how different cell types in the neocortex work together when psilocybin acts on the brain.
This project studies how diabetes during pregnancy changes blood-forming cells in the children born from those pregnancies.
This project studies the regulatory elements in fast-evolving duplicated regions of the genome and how they relate to human evolution and disease.
This project studies how the social networks and communication of young adult couples coping with cancer affect their relationship satisfaction, well-being and stress.
This project uses metagenomic sequencing of blood samples to find the microbes that cause sepsis and to predict how patients with sepsis will do.
This project studies how macrophages and other cells in blood vessel walls affect whether atherosclerotic plaque stays stable, using mouse models and human disease.
This project studies how different areas of the human cortex work together in step.
This project tries to find out whether inflammation drives chronic myelomonocytic leukemia to progress, and whether existing therapies can stop it.
This project refines a fluorescence guided imaging tool that shows blood flow in bone during surgery to help surgeons remove infected bone.
This project builds a tool that predicts the risk of early death in autistic older adults using existing Medicare claims data.
This project builds a gene editing toolkit to correct many disease-causing changes in a gene tied to cystic fibrosis.
